Living Well / Resource directory

Share a plan without creating confusion

Start with life

What would be useful?

Give participants one understandable account of what is agreed and what remains open.

The simpler starting point: A short message with confirmed details may be enough. Do not require another account for a task that does not need collaboration.

Finish when: The intended people can open the right version, understand permissions, and correct mistakes.

Choose by fit

Different tools, different jobs.

These are editorial comparisons based on public descriptions, not a ranking from hands-on tests. Choose one suitable route; using every option is not the goal.

Google Keep: collaboration basics

Consider it when: Everyone can use Keep and the task is a shared list.

Check first: Confirm how owner deletion and edits affect others.

Access: The guide is free to read. Using shared Keep notes requires suitable Google accounts and access to the service.

Open Google Keep: collaboration basics · Full context and source

Apple Notes: copy or collaborate

Consider it when: The participants already use compatible Apple devices.

Check first: Choose between sending a copy and collaborating in iCloud.

Access: Free instructions. Collaboration needs compatible Apple devices, Apple Accounts, and Notes enabled in iCloud.

Open Apple Notes: copy or collaborate · Full context and source

CryptPad: collaborative documents

Consider it when: A group wants to examine another document-sharing model.

Check first: Review the chosen host, ownership, retention, and access links.

Access: Free public documentation. Hosted service quotas, guest retention, accounts, and paid storage depend on the chosen instance.

Open CryptPad: collaborative documents · Full context and source

LocalSend: move a file nearby

Consider it when: You only need to move a file between nearby devices.

Check first: Confirm the recipient and remember that transfer is not live collaboration.

Access: Free open-source native apps on supported desktop and mobile platforms. Install on both devices and use a working local network.

Open LocalSend: move a file nearby · Full context and source

Living Room Conversations

Consider it when: What is missing is a thoughtful conversation rather than a better app.

Check first: Use questions as invitations, not as a script the other person must follow.

Access: Selected starter guides are available without login. The broader guide library requires a free account.

Explore Living Room Conversations · Full context and source

From choice to use

Keep the human purpose visible.

Do not turn suggestions into agreements

Mark a proposed time, conditional offer, or undecided venue as exactly that. A generated summary cannot supply consent.

Agree the maintenance

Name who updates the plan and which changes deserve a message. Provide an alternative for someone who cannot use the chosen service.

Check the human outcome

Ask whether coordination became clearer. Include the effort people spent learning the system or requesting access; convenience for the creator is not the whole result.

Published as a selection path, not a personal field note. Source dates and access limits belong to each resource. No paid placement or affiliation is implied.

Go a little further

Make the next step concrete.
